title: Jacques Perrault Honored with John S. Bates Medal at Paperweek 2025
text:
Jacques perrault Awarded​ the prestigious ‍John ​S. Bates Gold medal at PaperWeek 2025 in‍ Montreal.⁢ During ⁢the PaperWeek 2025 ⁣conference held in Montreal, Jacques Perrault was ​honored with the John S. Bates​ Memorial gold Medal, the⁢ highest distinction ​recognizing outstanding contributions, dedication, and‌ impact in the Canadian pulp and paper industry .
Jacques Perrault,‌ a chemical engineer with a degree from ‌Polytechnic in 1976, has devoted his career to optimizing and resolving challenges linked ​to paper‍ processes. He has worked for ​several large companies in the sector, ⁢including CIP, Domtar, Forest Products Alliance, Bowater, and Cascades,⁣ on‌ a ‌variety of ‍paper ‍grades ranging from newspaper and ‍specialty papers to ⁢fine paper and cardboard.
His‍ expertise also led him ‌to Black Clawson, a⁤ manufacturer of paper machines, where he contributed to the Top‌ Flyte program and played a key role in major projects such‌ as Dolbeau PM5, Donnacona PM4 , and‌ the conversion of the Bear Island Paper machine to‌ produce cardboard⁢ boxes.​ He was also actively involved in the start-up of emblematic machines such as Domtar Windsor PM7 and PM8 , and also Greenpac . ⁣Additionally, he developed ⁤a practical‌ guide to energy efficiency in paper manufacturing for Hydro-Québec .
Longtime member of CPPA, OIQ, PAPTAC, TAPPI, and IASPM associations, Jacques Perrault holds ‌a patent for an instrument measuring⁢ the rolling ‍of paper. His Excellency was‌ also recognized by the ​C. Howard Smith and Jasper ‍Mardon ⁣prices ⁣of ⁣PAPTAC.
The ⁣delivery of this distinction during PaperWeek 2025 offered a privileged opportunity to celebrate this recognition with his⁣ colleagues and industry professionals.
Jacques Perrault: Reflecting on a Lifetime of Contributions​ to the Canadian‍ Pulp and Paper Industry During the recent PaperWeek 2025 conference held⁢ in Montreal, Jacques Perrault, a chemical engineer with extensive experience in ⁣the Canadian pulp and paper industry, was honored with ⁢the John ​S. Bates Memorial⁤ Gold Medal, the highest distinction recognizing ⁣outstanding contributions,⁣ dedication, and impact. This recognition reflects⁣ Perrault’s dedication ⁣and ​extensive career in ⁣optimizing and resolving challenges ​linked to paper‌ processes.The ‌event offered a privileged opportunity to celebrate this recognition ‍with colleagues and industry professionals.
Career ⁣and⁤ Contributions to the Paper Industry Senior Editor: ⁣Could you tell ​us a ‍bit about your journey in the pulp and paper industry and how you ended up ‍working with companies like ‍Domtar, Forest Products Alliance, and Cascades?
Jacques Perrault: After⁤ graduating as ‍a chemical engineer from Polytechnic in 1976, I was blessed to work with​ several notable companies in ⁣the sector.‍ These included CIP, Domtar, Forest⁣ Products Alliance, Bowater, and Cascades.My career spanned various paper grades, from newspaper‌ and‌ specialty papers to fine paper and cardboard. Each project brought unique challenges and experiences, contributing to my expertise ⁤in optimizing ​paper processes.
Key Projects and Innovations Senior editor: You’ve been involved in some major projects, such as the Dolbeau PM5 and Donnacona PM4 installations. Could you share some insights into‍ these projects?
Jacques Perrault: Indeed, projects ​like Dolbeau PM5⁤ and⁤ Donnacona PM4 were⁢ significant milestones in my career.At Black Clawson,‍ I⁢ contributed ⁤to ‌the​ Top Flyte​ program and⁢ played a key role‍ in ⁣the conversion ⁣of the Bear Island Paper machine to produce cardboard boxes. These projects required a deep understanding of paper processing techniques and innovative problem-solving, which I​ was glad⁢ to bring to the​ table.
Inventions and ​Recognition Senior Editor: Alongside your industry contributions, you’ve also received notable recognitions and hold a patent for an instrument measuring the rolling of‍ paper. Could‍ you elaborate‍ on this?
Jacques perrault: Yes,⁢ I⁣ have ‍been fortunate to receive several recognitions, including the C. Howard Smith and Jasper Mardon prices from PAPTAC. ‌one of my notable contributions‍ is​ a patent for an instrument that ​measures the rolling of paper. ⁤This ⁣invention stemmed from my dedication to​ improving paper process efficiency and quality,reflecting my ongoing​ involvement and passion for innovation in the industry.
The Role of Associations Senior Editor: You’ve been a longtime member of various associations ‌like CPPA, OIQ, PAPTAC, TAPPI, and IASPM. How have these associations helped⁤ in your career advancement?
Jacques Perrault: Membership in these associations‍ has ‍been invaluable for networking, learning, and ⁤staying current ⁤with industry⁤ trends. These‍ associations provide platforms for sharing⁢ knowledge and best⁢ practices,which have considerably contributed to my⁤ professional growth. They also offer opportunities to collaborate ⁤with peers, enhancing my understanding‍ and request of ‌industry technologies and methodologies.
Jacques ‌Perrault’s unprecedented success ⁢in optimizing paper processes and ⁤his ⁤contributions to major ‍projects within the Canadian pulp and paper industry are testament to ⁣his commitment ⁢and expertise. His⁢ work continues to inspire and influence the sector,⁢ and his recognition‍ with the John‍ S. Bates Memorial Gold Medal is a⁤ well-deserved honor.
